title: Hyperdimensional Vector Tsetlin Machines with Applications to Sequence Learning and Generation
new_feature: Two-layer HVTM: hyperdimensional binary-spatter-code encoding of sequences (interval embedding, N-gram binding, bundling) feeding a weighted clause-sharing TM with a max-literals cap; used for UCR time-series classification and, combined with HV associative memory, for forecasting and generating sequences.

datasets.name_in_paper: UCR Time Series Classification archive (128 data sets)
datasets.input_shape_or_features: 128 univariate datasets, varying lengths (24 to >500) and classes
datasets.split_as_reported: official UCR train/test splits presumably (not explicitly stated); sizes vary per dataset
datasets.booleanization: HV encoding: interval embedding (Q buckets -> random HVs), N-gram binding with cyclic-shift position vectors (XOR), majority bundling into one binary HV of dimension D; D=5000, N-gram=3, Q=50
datasets.notes: Results per dataset only in scatter/bar figures (Figs. 4-6).

extraction_notes: UCR results only as aggregate statement (~78% of datasets within 2 pp of best ED/DTW benchmark) plus figures; no per-dataset numbers extracted and baseline numbers not tabulated. Forecast Table 1: value = mean error, std_or_range = standard error as labelled. The error metric is not precisely defined (the text suggests an RMS-like error over 24 steps with upper bound sqrt(48)/24... ). 'Sparse TM' listed because the max-literals-per-clause mechanism of the Sparse TM paper is used. Training sizes for synthetic series not fully stated.
